audit-options-help-debug-action-make-a-p: Actual Qt recording forwards the real CallLater/background SingleJob and messagepublication and observes real elapsed 5054.124/6002.523ms. Native tests inject this owner clock and call the production tick at 4999/5000/5999/6000ms; these prove deadline admission/order/noearly publication, not physical five-second native timer latency or equality of Qt/native timestamps.

The real native earliest-deadline weak single-shot timer rechecks the monotonic clock and polls owner/dismissal liveness at most 200ms; event-loop delivery can occur later. The actual 250ms popup projection timer is exercised only for Show resumption after durable hidden publication.

Hidden Main refuses new admission while already-admitted deadlines publish to Store; hidden cards remain frozen until Show refresh. Durable native Store jobs/reopen are explicit native behavior, not a claim that Qt persists its transient JobStatus cards.

Exit Cancel, accepted exit, same Main rebind, sole Bound owner drop and hide-before-drop actual Main destruction are separate native regressions; retained old controls cannot resurrect. General multiple-owner/lost-window/event-loop failure combinations are not exhaustively covered.

Store read/write errors retire pending producer work by source, consuming no duplicate deadline; there is no dedicated injected producer Store failure regression. No failure-notification wording parity is claimed.

The actual Qt PNG is a manager crop with two simple cards and “2 messages”/“dismiss all” summary; the native capture is full Main after real Show refresh. This supports card/text/state comparison, not pixel/frame geometry identity or a screenshot proving elapsed deadline.
Only the original make-a-popup-in-five-seconds leaf is selected; other Debug actions, long-popup producer completion or modal/new-page actions receive no extra completion credit.
Windows and macOS are deferred; this preparation and required publication validation are Linux-only.

The weak-window and Owner-drop regressions prove producer retirement without retaining Main. Retained Control handles still own their State and Store until those handles are dropped; this packet does not claim immediate release of every Store owner on GUI retirement.

The current 1000×700 full Main capture shows two complete exact-message cards and “2 messages”/“dismiss all” summary; Qt records its cropped manager. This is after-show consumer evidence, not a picture of physical five-second scheduling.
audit-options-speed-and-memory-download-: Linux-only validation at the exact source/run/artifact; Windows and macOS are deferred. Approval covers this original leaf only, with no broader parent, alias or unrelated completion credit.

All eight fresh shared helper PNGs were actually inspected. Estimates, warnings and numeric controls are separate at all four sizes, including the wrapped long warning; lower rows fall below the normal ScrollView fold. Shared layout evidence does not widen the defining consumer claim.
Only visible current-page status list/totals scheduling is claimed. Importer, daemon and network work remain unchanged; no background cadence or throughput parity is inferred.

The native binding owns a 250 ms Slint timer and synchronous Store status snapshots. It uses the reference strict wall-clock deadline comparison; saved changes affect the next period without resetting the pending deadline. Cache expiry uses a separate monotonic clock.

Qt records actual paused private importer managers with 0/3/12 displayed rows and a restored synthetic clock, without real network traffic. Native timer tests use 12 paused queues; other row-count, negative and zero-denominator histories are model replays.

Qt captures only the default timing box (1 s / 30 for both kinds), while native gallery controls show 333 ms / 7.
